title: AgentTime: Can Agents Estimate and Control Their Own Runtime?
abstract: arXiv:2610.09944v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: An essential control of AI agents is their ability to manage runtime. This ability requires a sense of time-awareness, to predict and estimate wall-clock time and to control their own actions. Prior work has focused on time-awareness, but duration-following and control in native agent harnesses remain unexplored. We present AgentTime, a benchmark for testing whether agents can work for a requested duration, predict their runtime, and estimate elapsed time afterward. It comprises 222 tasks from 18 sources spanning coding, computer use, agentic work, and automated research. Duration-following experiments append a single instruction specifying how long to work, with requests ranging from about a minute to multiple days. translated_title: AgentTime：智能体能否估计和控制自身的运行时间？
translated_abstract: 管理运行时间是AI智能体的一项基本控制能力。这种能力需要时间感知意识，以便预测和估计实际耗时（墙上时钟时间）并控制自身的行为。以往的工作主要关注时间感知，但在原生智能体框架中遵循指定时长及运行时间控制的能力仍未被探索。我们提出了AgentTime，这是一个用于测试智能体能否按请求时长工作、预测自身运行时间以及事后估计已用时间的基准。该基准包含来自18个来源的222个任务，涵盖编程、计算机使用、智能体工作和自动化研究等领域。在时长遵循实验中，仅需附加一条说明工作时长的指令，请求时长从约一分钟到数天不等。模型在这些指令上的准确性差异显著：在Claude Code中的Fable 5.1偏离请求运行时间的典型倍数达2.9倍，而在Codex中的GPT-6 Astra仅为1.2倍。然而，匹配……（摘要不完整）
tldr: 提出了AgentTime基准，用于测试智能体能否按要求时长工作、预测运行时间和事后估计已用时间，发现不同模型的时长遵循能力差异显著（偏差从1.2倍到2.9倍不等）。
en_tdlr: AgentTime is a benchmark testing whether agents can work for requested durations, predict their runtime, and estimate elapsed time, revealing substantial variation in duration-following accuracy across models (deviations from 1.2× to 2.9×).
